- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect downward pressure.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–5 days; apply downward bias of 1–3% to subsequent forecasts.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model lags in adjusting; delay or reduce forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model tends to overfit short-term volatility; for 30-day forecasts, apply smoothing or mean-reversion bias if true outcome deviates >2% from 14-day moving average.
